title: The Research Process: Problem Statement, Objectives, Literature Review
summary: Formulating the research problem; aims and objectives; purpose and steps of literature review; background and gap identification.
objectives: List the steps of the research process.
Explain how to formulate a research problem.
Describe the purpose of a literature review.
revision: Research process: problem → literature review → hypothesis → design. Objectives are specific and measurable.
traps: A problem statement is framed as a question, not a statement.
confusions: Skipping literature review before hypothesis formulation.

notes.t: A problem statement is always framed as a question because it helps to clearly define what needs to be explored or solved. It guides the direction of research or inquiry. A good problem statement asks something specific and researchable.

r: Defining what needs to be explored or solved.
Planning how the study will be conducted.

notes.t: The aim or objective explains what the researcher wants to achieve through the study. It gives a clear focus and direction. Objectives are specific, measurable and aligned with the problem statement.

i: Builds a background for your research.
Helps identify gaps in existing studies.
Guides the choice of research method.
Supports and strengthens the problem statement.

notes.t: The research process flows from problem statement to literature review to hypothesis to research design. A problem statement is always framed as a question.

mnemonics.title: PLHD
mnemonics.text: P — Problem formulation, L — Literature review, H — Hypothesis development, D — Design preparation

flashcards.q: What is the first step in the research process?
What is the purpose of a literature review?
flashcards.a: Builds background, identifies gaps, guides method choice, strengthens the problem statement.
